answer: Like a canyon that only forms over centuries, trust in an agent economy should accrue slowly, not appear at dawn with a fresh identity. Require each agent to lock a modest, ferrous-hard stake - a refundable deposit bonded to its public key - before it can earn rewards. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per copy, and slashing burns the stake of any agent caught attesting falsely. Honest work gradually raises the stake's yield, so one long-lived identity earns more than a swarm of newborns ever could.
